subject: Retro Usage Clarification & Mop-up Charge Plan for Q2 Expansion
messages:
From: Katie Chen <katie.chen@averysys.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@averysys.com
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q2 capacity increase - invoice / retro charge question

Hi Marcus,

Hope you're doing well. We did a mid-quarter scale-up on June 3 to handle a campaign spike and the usage report shows a ~38% increase in inference hours that month. Our finance team is seeing a retroactive charge on the draft invoice for the extra capacity and they asked whether that can be split across next two invoices rather than billed as a single one-time line item.

Can you confirm:
- What triggered the retroactive charge (was it an auto-topup or a consumption true-up?)
- Whether Redwood can amortize the one-off over 2 months or else apply a small credit to smooth the impact

I attached the usage report and the draft invoice PDF from our side. We want to avoid a surprise one-off to the GL. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if easier.

Thanks,
Katie
Billing Operations
Avery Systems

Attachments: Avery_Q2_usage_report.csv (csv, 48KB), draft_invoice_avery_q2.pdf (pdf, 122KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Katie Chen <katie.chen@averysys.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 capacity increase - invoice / retro charge question

Hi Katie — thanks for the note and the report. Short answer: the line is a true-up for auto-topup-enabled Dedicated capacity that kicked in May 29 when your throughput threshold was exceeded; the platform automatically allocated burst capacity which is billed on consumption with a retroactive reconciliation.

Longer answer / proposed options:
1) One-time retro invoice (what's on the draft): immediate settlement, reflected on this month's invoice.
2) Amortize: we can split the one-off into two equal line items spread over the next two invoices (no finance fee).
3) Apply a smoothing credit: Redwood can provide a one-time 10% smoothing credit on the retro line to reduce the net impact.

I want to be transparent about approvals: option 2 (amortize) requires sign-off from finance (Ben) for the accounting treatment and option 3 (credit) needs manager approval for promotional credits (Grace). I've looped them here and asked them to confirm. If you prefer, we can do option 2 + a smaller 5% credit.

Proposed next step: if either amortize or credit works, I can send an updated invoice draft by end of week and tag the HubSpot deal so your AP team sees the change. If you need a formal statement for your GL, we can also provide a short memo explaining the true-up cause and dates.

-Marcus
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_mopup_invoice_draft.pdf (pdf, 38KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 capacity increase - invoice / retro charge question

Marcus / Grace — saw the thread and the usage CSV. Finance is okay with amortizing the retro charge over two invoices provided two conditions are met:
- Customer signs the amended invoice terms (one-line amendment in HubSpot / DocuSign)
- The amortization is clearly labeled in the invoices for audit trail (we'll use GL code 4012-RTR).

Regarding the 10% smoothing credit, I recommend capping to 5% for the one-off in this case since the overage was driven by an unplanned campaign and the account is otherwise current. Approving 10% is fine for strategic upsells but let's keep margins in mind.

I'll prepare the amended invoice language and a short accounting memo. Marcus — send me the final retro amount and preferred amortization schedule (split dates). Grace — can you sign off on the customer-facing credit once I post the doc?

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 16:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 capacity increase - invoice / retro charge question

Thanks Ben. Approved: amortize over next two invoices and apply a 5% goodwill credit on the retro principal. We want to preserve the upsell motion but avoid setting an easy precedent for deep comping. Marcus, go ahead and update the invoice and send Katie the revised draft with the amended terms PDF and DocuSign link. Make the HubSpot note "Amortize retro charge over 2 invoices; 5% credit applied; GL 4012-RTR."

- Grace
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
